awarding_body.value: American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), the credentialing affiliate of the American Nurses Association (ANA); credential developed in partnership with the American Academy of Ambulatory Care Nursing (AAACN)

year_launched.value_detail: First Ambulatory Care Nursing certification exam administered by ANCC in October 1999; 92 nurses took the inaugural exam. Credential acronym was RN-BC until ANCC's COC re-acronym project replaced it with AMB-BC.

credential_rename.value_detail: ANCC's Commission on Board Certification (COC) updated specialty credential acronyms to disambiguate each specialty; RN-BC for ambulatory care became AMB-BC. Older RN-BC holders may still see RN-BC on legacy credentials.

eligibility.value: Active RN license in US/territory or legally recognized equivalent in another country; 2 years full-time equivalent RN practice; 2,000 hours of clinical practice in ambulatory care nursing within the last 3 years; 30 hours of continuing education in ambulatory care nursing within the last 3 years.

exam_format_primary_source.value: 150 questions total — 125 scored + 25 pretest — 3-hour computer-based test, year-round at Prometric centers in a 120-day window.
exam_format_primary_source.notes: Both the current TCO effective 2021-05-01 (last updated 2025-09-03) and the upcoming TCO effective 2026-09-11 state 150 questions / 125 scored.

exam_format_certs_js.notes: Conflict with ANCC primary source — see discrepancies block. certs.js wins per project rule (hero pill = 175). ANCC primary 150/125/25 is surfaced in at-a-glance + blueprint.

passing_score.notes: ANCC reports pass/fail with diagnostic feedback for each content area. Scaled-score detail is widely cited but not on a single ANCC URL we could verify.

fee_ana_member.notes: ANA members pay $295 (price includes $140 non-refundable administrative fee).

fee_retake.value: $270 flat fee for everyone (no discounts apply)
fee_retake.notes: From AAACN fact sheet (most recent published reference). ANCC main page does not surface a separate retake-fee line.

test_delivery.value: Computer-based at Prometric test centers, year-round, 120-day testing window after Authorization to Test (ATT). Effective September 11, 2026 the Test Content Outline and Reference List are updated; a 7-business-day suspension (Aug 28 to Sep 10, 2026) brackets the swap. Candidates can test BEFORE August 28th, 2026 or AFTER September 10th, 2026.

renewal_rules.value: Two pathways. Option A (Professional Development + Practice Hours): hold current active RN license + current ANCC certification, complete the certification specialty's professional development requirements within the 5-year cycle, complete 1,000 practice hours in the certification role/specialty within the 5-year cycle, and pay the renewal fee. Option B (Professional Development + Testing): same prerequisites minus the practice-hours requirement, but the candidate must pass the current certification exam. Renewal applications may be submitted up to 12 months prior to expiration.

retake_rules.value: May retest after 60 calendar days from the date last tested. May not test more than three times in any 12-month period. Wait at least 5 days after the examination before submitting a retest application. Retest applications are reviewed as unique applications subject to eligibility rules in effect at the time of retest application.

accreditation.value: ABSNC accredited (Accreditation Board for Specialty Nursing Certification)

first_year_cohort.value_detail: 92 nurses took the first ANCC Ambulatory Care Nursing certification exam in October 1999.

active_certificants.value_detail: Total certified as of 12/31/2025 per ANCC 2025 Certification Data PDF.

common_confusions.value: Most commonly confused with: (1) legacy RN-BC Ambulatory Care — the prior acronym for the same credential, now AMB-BC; older nurses may still hold or display RN-BC. (2) Care Coordination & Transition Management Certification (CCTM, ANCC, renewal only) — adjacent ambulatory specialty focused on care-coordination workflows. (3) Telehealth Nursing Certification (NTI-BC via NCC; AAACN-aligned) — separate exam focused on telephone triage and telehealth nursing; AMB-BC includes telehealth content but is broader. (4) Medical-Surgical Nursing Board Certified (MEDSURG-BC, ANCC) — inpatient acute-care specialty; AMB-BC is the outpatient/clinic counterpart. (5) Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP-BC, ANCC) — APRN credential, not an RN specialty exam.

salary_context_bls.value: BLS OEWS (May 2024) reports a national mean RN wage of $98,430 and median $93,600. Ambulatory-care RN sub-aggregates (vendor-curated): mean roughly $94,480/yr ($45.42/hr); outpatient care centers average ~$102,640/yr.
salary_context_bls.notes: BLS does not publish a separate AMB-BC certified wage; salary detail uses BLS OEWS plus the ambulatory-care sub-aggregate reported by NursingEducation.org from BLS data.

tco_change_2026.value: Effective 2026-09-11 the Test Content Outline and Reference List are updated. ANCC suspends scheduling for 7 business days (Aug 28 – Sep 10, 2026) to swap the exam. Candidates must test BEFORE Aug 28, 2026 or AFTER Sep 10, 2026. The new outline keeps 150 items / 125 scored and the four-domain structure; weights shift slightly (Assess and Evaluate 41% vs prior 40%; Plan and Implement 16% vs 18%; Professional Role 24% vs 22%; Education unchanged at 19%) and domain titles update (Assessment and Diagnosis; Planning and Implementation; Evaluation and Modification; Patient and Community Education).

blueprint.notes: Current TCO effective 2021-05-01, last updated 2025-09-03. Includes disease process, medications, preventative care, expected outcomes (knowledge); treatment evaluation, triage (in-person/virtual/telehealth), physical and psychosocial assessment, clinical data interpretation (skill).
Care coordination, disease-specific interventions (knowledge); clinical tasks — procedures, point-of-care testing, wound care (skill).
Scope and standards (ANA, AAACN, legal/regulatory), professional development, fiscal health (knowledge); advocacy, leadership, safety and security (skill).
Modes of educational delivery, diverse populations, communication barriers (knowledge); professional communication (skill).

blueprint_2026_post_tco_change.domain: Assess and Evaluate (renamed: Assessment and Diagnosis)
Plan and Implement (renamed: Planning and Implementation)

pass_rate_history.notes: ANCC 2025 Certification Data PDF — first-time test takers; Ambulatory Care Nursing row.
AAACN fact sheet (older snapshot — 3,268 certificants as of 12/2016).

discrepancies.resolution: certs.js wins per project canonical-source rule. Hero pill shows 175. At-a-glance + blueprint surfaces the ANCC primary source (150 total / 125 scored / 25 pretest) and explains the legacy 2017 outline used 175 items / 150 scored. The current TCO (effective 2021-05-01, last updated 2025-09-03) and the upcoming TCO (effective 2026-09-11) both state 150/125/25.

discrepancies.issue: Scaled score 350 on a 0–500 scale is widely reported by third-party prep vendors but is not surfaced as a numeric pass-mark on the ANCC AMB-BC product page. ANCC reports pass/fail with diagnostic content-area feedback.
discrepancies.resolution: Surface the scaled-score description in at-a-glance with a 'reported by third-party prep vendors' caveat in the page prose, and link to the ANCC scores-and-retest page for primary authority on pass/fail reporting.
